saw_lines: Teachers buy classroom material the week before a unit starts, then reorder when the next level book comes out.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a busy teacher decides if your ad is about their lesson.
Your 30 live ads carry no proof number, so new buyers have nothing concrete to trust. Put one real figure, like your review count, on the next batch’s creative.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 12 Nov 2026
points: None of your 30 live ads shows a proof number, so new buyers have nothing concrete to trust. Collect one real figure, like your review count or orders shipped, and put it on the creative of the next batch.
0 of 30 ads carry an offer, so a teacher who never bought has no reason to act today. Open the next three ads with a first order discount or a trial month, and test them against your current copy.

8 ads have run 60+ days, yet none of the 22 newer ads reuses their opening line, so the proof never carries forward. Build the next three ads as variations of your oldest winner, keeping its opening and changing the second line.

24 openings across 30 copy ads, and the biggest opens just 2, so no story gets enough variations to learn from. Pick the two strongest, such as Love2Teach free materials and the teacher subscription, and build the next batch from them.
